solution.description: Read the problem as an indefinite integral of the single term 3x to the fourth power, taken with respect to x.

solution.operation: Apply the power rule for integration
solution.description: Recall the standard rule: integrating a times x to the n gives a times x to the n plus 1, divided by n plus 1, plus an arbitrary constant c. It is valid for any power except n equal to minus 1.
Match the term 3x to the fourth against the pattern a times x to the n, which fixes a as 3 and n as 4.
Raise the exponent from 4 to 5, divide by that new exponent 5, keep the coefficient 3 in place, and add the constant of integration.
Write the coefficient as three fifths in front of x to the fifth. Nothing more can be cancelled, so this is the final form.
The constant factor four ninths is carried outside, and the power rule is applied to t cubed: add 1 to the exponent and divide by the new exponent.
Work out the raised exponent and the new divisor, so the bracket becomes t to the fourth over 4.
Cancel the 4 in the bracket against the 4 in four ninths, leaving one ninth of t to the fourth plus c.
Rewrite 2 divided by x squared as 2 times x to the minus 2, so the integrand becomes a single power term that the power rule can handle.
Apply the power rule with a equal to 2 and n equal to minus 2: add 1 to the exponent and divide by that new exponent.
Evaluate minus 2 plus 1 as minus 1, both in the exponent and in the denominator.
Dividing by minus 1 flips the sign, and x to the minus 1 is 1 over x, so the integral is minus 2 over x plus c.
Rewrite the square root of x as x to the power one half, so the power rule applies to it.
Apply the power rule with n equal to one half: add 1 to the exponent and divide by the new exponent.
Simplify one half plus 1 to three halves, in the exponent and in the denominator alike.
Dividing by three halves is the same as multiplying by two thirds, and x to the three halves is the square root of x cubed, giving two thirds of the square root of x cubed plus c.
Integrating the constant 8 is the n equal to zero case of the power rule, so it gives 8x plus the constant of integration.
The same reasoning applies to the constant 5 with respect to t, giving 5t plus c. Only the letter of the variable changes.

key_reminders: {'point': 'Remember: Integration reverses differentiation.'}
{'point': "Always add the arbitrary constant 'c' when performing indefinite integration, because the derivative of any constant is zero."}
{'point': 'Note: The differential coefficient $\\frac{dy}{dx}$ indicates differentiation with respect to x; in integration, the variable is specified by dx, dt, etc.'}
{'point': 'Caution: The formula $\\int ax^n dx = \\frac{ax^{n+1}}{n+1} + c$ applies only when $n \\ne -1$.'}
{'point': 'Speed tip: Recognize common forms — e.g., integral of constant is kx + c — to solve quickly.'}
common_mistakes: Forgetting the arbitrary constant c on an indefinite integral.
Dividing by the old exponent instead of the new one, for example writing 3x^5/4 in part (i).
Losing the minus sign in part (iii): dividing by -1 makes the answer -2/x, not 2/x.

concept.technique_name: evaluating divisions and expressions to a stated accuracy

examples.problem_statement: Problem 1. Evaluate 364.7 ÷ 57.5 correct to 3 decimal places

solution.description: State the division to be evaluated: 364.7 shared into groups of 57.5, to three decimal places.

solution.operation: Eliminate decimals by multiplying both numbers by 10
solution.description: Multiplying both numbers by 10 clears the decimal points without changing the value of the quotient, turning the sum into 3647 divided by 575.
Ask how many whole times 575 fits into 3647. Six times gives 3450, and seven times would overshoot.

solution.operation: Subtract and bring down the next digit
solution.description: Subtract 3450 from 3647, leaving a remainder of 197. So far the quotient is 6.

solution.operation: Add decimal point and zeros for decimal places
solution.description: Place the decimal point in the quotient and attach three zeros to the remainder, so the division can continue past the units place.
Bring down the first zero to make 1970. Three lots of 575 give 1725, the largest multiple that fits, so the first decimal digit is 3.

solution.operation: Subtract and bring down next zero
solution.description: Subtract 1725 from 1970, leaving 245, and bring down the next zero.
With 2450 to divide, four lots of 575 give 2300, so the second decimal digit is 4.

solution.operation: Subtract and bring down next zero
solution.description: Subtract 2300 from 2450, leaving 150, and bring down the last zero.
With 1500 to divide, two lots of 575 give 1150, so the third decimal digit is 2.
Subtract 1150 from 1500, leaving 350. The division has been carried far enough to decide the third decimal place.

solution.operation: Combine results and round to 3 decimal places
solution.description: Assemble the digits found: 6 point 3 4 2 and more to come. The next digit makes the quotient 6.3432, which rounds to 6.343 at three decimal places.

examples.problem_statement: Problem 2. Evaluate (12.47 × 31.59)/(70.45 × 0.052) correct to 4 significant figures

solution.description: Key in 12.47, the first factor of the numerator.
Press the multiply key so the calculator will multiply 12.47 by whatever is entered next.
Key in 31.59 to complete the numerator product.
Press divide, so everything entered from here on is treated as the divisor.

solution.operation: The denominator must have brackets; i.e. press (.
solution.description: Open a bracket first, because the whole product below the line is the divisor, not just its first factor.

solution.operation: Type in 70.45 × 0.052 and complete the bracket; i.e. ).
solution.description: Key both denominator factors inside the bracket and close it, grouping 70.45 times 0.052 as a single divisor.
Press equals to evaluate the whole expression. The display shows 107.530518..., which is 107.5 to four significant figures.

examples.problem_statement: Determine the area enclosed by $y=2x+3$, the x-axis and ordinates $x=1$ and $x=4$

solution.description: The area between the line, the x-axis and the two ordinates is found by integrating the function between those two x values.
Integrate term by term: 2x becomes x squared and 3 becomes 3x. The constant of integration is carried for now, but it cancels in a definite integral.

solution.operation: Apply the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
solution.description: Write the antiderivative in square brackets with the limits 1 and 4 attached, ready for substitution.
Substitute the upper limit x equal to 4 into x squared plus 3x, giving 16 plus 12, that is 28.
Substitute the lower limit x equal to 1 into the same expression, giving 1 plus 3, that is 4.
Subtract the lower-limit value from the upper-limit value: 28 minus 4 is 24 square units.

examples.problem_statement: Find distance travelled by a body with velocity $v = (2t^2 + 5)$ m/s from $t=0$ to $t=4$ s

solution.description: Distance travelled is the integral of velocity over time, so integrate 2t squared plus 5 from t equal to 0 to t equal to 4.
Integrate term by term with the power rule: 2t squared becomes two thirds of t cubed and 5 becomes 5t, written in square brackets with the limits.
Substitute the upper limit t equal to 4, where t cubed is 64, and subtract the lower-limit value at t equal to 0, which is zero. That leaves 128 over 3 plus 20.
Write 20 as 60 over 3 so both terms share a denominator, then add to get 188 over 3, about 62.67 metres.

key_reminders: {'point': 'Remember: If a curve drops below the x-axis, the integral becomes negative — place a minus sign before the integral for area calculation.'}
{'point': 'Note: Total shaded area is not the same as $\\int_a^d f(x)\\,dx$ when the curve crosses the x-axis.'}
{'point': 'It is usually necessary to sketch a curve to check whether it crosses the x-axis.'}
{'point': '(This answer may be checked since the shaded area is a trapezium...)'}
common_mistakes: Evaluating the antiderivative at the upper limit only and forgetting to subtract the lower-limit value.
Adding 128/3 and 20 without first writing 20 as 60/3.

solution.description: The shaded area is given as the integral of y with respect to x from 0 to pi over 3, and here y is sin 2x.

solution.operation: Apply the integral formula for sin(ax)
solution.description: Use the standard result that the integral of sin of a x is minus one over a, times cos of a x. In this problem a is 2.
Write the antiderivative, minus one half cos 2x, in square brackets with the limits 0 and pi over 3 attached.
Substitute the upper limit. The angle doubles to 2 pi over 3, whose cosine is minus one half, and minus one half times minus one half gives one quarter.
Substitute the lower limit. The angle doubles to 0, cos 0 is 1, so the value here is minus one half.

solution.operation: Subtract lower limit from upper limit
solution.description: Subtract the lower value from the upper: one quarter minus minus one half is one quarter plus one half, giving three quarters of a square unit.

common_mistakes: Writing the integral of sin 2x as -cos 2x and dropping the factor of one half.
Taking cos(2 pi / 3) as positive one half; it is negative, since the angle lies in the second quadrant.
Subtracting the upper value from the lower, which reverses the sign of the area.

solution.description: The expression 3.57 pi means 3.57 multiplied by pi, so treat it as a product before evaluating.
Replace pi by its decimal value 3.1415926535 and more, turning the problem into ordinary decimal multiplication.

Multiply 3.57 by the remaining decimal part of pi, which gives about 0.5054857.
Add the two partial products to recover the full value, about 11.2154857.
The third decimal digit is 5, so rounding to two decimal places gives 11.22.

examples.problem_statement: The volume V cm³ of a right circular cone is given by V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h. Given that radius r = 2.45 cm and height h = 18.7 cm, find the volume, correct to 4 significant figures

solution.operation: Write the formula for volume of a cone
solution.description: Start from the standard formula for the volume of a right circular cone.
Substitute the given radius 2.45 cm and height 18.7 cm in place of r and h.
Square the radius first, since r squared is the innermost part of the expression: 2.45 squared is 6.0025.
Multiply that squared radius by the height, giving 112.24675.
Multiply by pi, using 3.1415926535, which gives about 352.633575.
Take a third of that product to finish the formula, giving about 117.544525 cubic centimetres.
The first four significant figures are 1, 1, 7 and 5, and the next digit is 4, so the value rounds down to 117.5 cubic centimetres.

examples.answer: force F = 1.49 × 10^{-11} newtons, correct to 3 significant figures
